https://www.ica.art/films/the-girls-4k-r.description: Sumitra Peries’ groundbreaking Sri Lankan film offers a tender and transporting journey through young dreams and first loves. Kusum, a poor but studious village girl who cleans the house of a wealthy family, sparks a connection with Nimal, the family’s prized son. Soma, Kusum’s younger sister, pursues beauty pageants and dreams of acting, believing it’s her best chance of a better life. What unfolds is a lyrical and poignant coming of age story, brimming with yearning and feminine sensibility. Sumitra Peries, known as ‘the poetess of Sri Lankan cinema’, became the country’s first female director with this astonishing debut. She draws out natural, affecting performances from her cast, particularly Vasanthi Chathurani, who was still at school when she played Kusum – the role that launched a long screen career.

https://www.ica.art/films/rosebush-pruni.description: Underneath the Catalonian sun, a rich white American family lives in hedonistic isolation, seeking love and validation through one another, their designer wardrobes and pop music. When an outsider infiltrates the family, buried tensions surface and blood ties are severed. An outrageous, biting satire on the absurdity of the patriarchal family, starring Callum Turner, Riley Keough, Jamie Bell, Lukas Gage, Elena Anaya, Tracy Letts, Elle Fanning and Pamela Anderson.

https://www.ica.art/films/the-day-she-re.description: The Day She Returns follows actress Bae Jeongsu (Song Sunmi), who, having stepped back from acting after marriage and a subsequent divorce, returns to the profession with a role in an independent film. As the film’s release approaches, she takes part in a series of press interviews. A subtle meditation on memory and performance, Hong Sangsoo's latest film unfolds through a series of increasingly intimate conversations, as he continues his exploration of the boundaries between lived experience and artistic creation.

https://www.ica.art/films/dry-leaf.description: Lisa, a sports photographer, has gone missing. She was last seen photographing rural football stadiums in villages across Georgia. Her father, Irakli, embarks on a journey in search of her, with the help of Lisa’s mysterious best friend. Shot on an old Sony Ericsson phone, Alexandre Koberidze's follow up to What Do We See When We Look at the Sky? is a remarkable exploration of absence and an endlessly intriguing journey through the Georgian countryside.

https://www.ica.art/films/birds-of-war.director: Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak
https://www.ica.art/films/birds-of-war.description: Janay Boulos, a young Lebanese journalist at the BBC, first contacts Syrian cameraman Abd Alkader Habak for footage during the final months of one of the bloodiest and most decisive turning points in Syria’s brutal civil war. Through texts, video exchanges, voice messages and shared moments from afar, their bond deepens as Janay discovers more about the extraordinary young man documenting violence for her reports, whilst Habak’s world becomes increasingly perilous. When an act of compassion forces Habak to flee Syria, their relationship enters a new phase: for the first time, they meet in person. Distance, war, cultural differences and familial judgements temporarily fade as the two wrap themselves in a cocoon of safety, away from the terror back home. Despite this, they are never far from the question that will soon enough come to haunt them: could two people from such disparate worlds build a life together?

https://www.ica.art/films/nostalgia-4k.description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s unforgettably haunting film, his first to be made outside Russia, explores the melancholy of the expatriate through the journey of Gorchakov, a Russian poet researching in Italy. Arriving at a Tuscan village spa with Eugenia, his Italian interpreter, Gorchakov is visited by memories of Russia and of his wife and children, as he encounters the local mystic who sets him a challenging task. Filled with a series of mysterious and extraordinary images, all of which coalesce into a miraculous whole in the film’s final shot, Nostalgia , is, as with so much of Tarkovsky's work, a film in which nature, the elements of fire and water, music, painting and poetry all play a major role.

https://www.ica.art/films/as-meninas-exe.description: Directed by Portugese filmmaker João Botelho, As Meninas Exemplares is whimsical ode to childhood, inspired by the painter Paula Rego and based on the writing of the Russian writer, the Countess of Ségur, known for her seminal children's books which depicted a turbulent kingdom of women. Botelho brings together a motley crew of women to play the Countess's heroines: the good, deceitful, cruel – and most importantly, the rebellious, with sensual and tender theatricality.

https://www.ica.art/films/blue-heron.description: Set on Vancouver Island in the late 1990s, Blue Heron follows eight - year-old Sasha and her Hungarian immigrant family as they attempt to build a new life, only to be destabilised by the increasingly dangerous behaviour of her older brother, Jeremy. Drawing on her own memories, filmmaker Sophy Romvari shapes a deeply personal portrait of childhood, family fractures, and the fragility of recollection.

https://www.ica.art/films/synthetic-sinc.description: The Synthetic Sincerity Lab based at the University of Southern England are trying to create authentic AI characters as part of a new research project. The head of the lab Professor SonG, licences the films of Marc Isaacs' to better understand what his AI characters are lacking and, in turn, agrees the Filmmaker can document their working process. Blending documentary with fiction, Synthetic Sincerity uses humour and innovative narrative techniques to form a reflection on what is happening to the human face in the era of AI and what this might mean for the future of cinema.

https://www.ica.art/films/rozier-fifi-ma.description: When a director (Mike Marshall) decides – out of pure superstition – to overhaul his play after a successful six month run he unwittingly instigates changes that appear to doom the production. Enter, by pure coincidence, Gaston (Jean Lefebvre), friend of star Fifi (Lili Vonderfeld) and owner of a near-perfect memory that allows him to quickly assume one of the play’s major roles. Filled to the brim with punning wordplay, theatrical allusions, and the delicious chaos of backstage maneuvering, Fifi Martingale is perhaps Rozier’s finest comedic take on the wild digressions and nick-of-time improvisations that comprise both art and life.

https://www.ica.art/films/rozier-from-on.description: Jacques Rozier’s filmmaking stands out for its originality, innovation, and nonconformity. Emmanuel Barnault's documentary delves into Rozier’s impromptu creativity and direct approach offering a captivating look at the enduring relevance and influence of his work in contemporary cinema.

https://www.ica.art/films/the-sacrifice-.description: Andrei Tarkovsky’s visionary final film unfolds in the hours before a nuclear holocaust. Among many other awards, The Sacrifice won the Cannes Grand Prix in 1986, the same year that Tarkovsky died of cancer in Paris at the age of 54. Erland Josephson, in an award-winning role, plays retired actor Alexander who is celebrating his birthday with family and friends when a crackly TV announcement warns of an imminent nuclear catastrophe. Alexander makes a promise to God that he will sacrifice all he holds dear if the disaster can be averted. The next day dawns and, as if in a dream, everything is restored to normality. But Alexander must keep his vow.

https://www.ica.art/films/ish.description: Set and filmed in the South Asian and Middle Eastern community in Luton, Ish follows 12-year-old best friends, Ish (Farhan Hasnat) and Maram (Yahya Kitana) who are navigating childhood against a backdrop of political tension and personal loss. After a police stop and search, where Maram is searched and Ish manages to run away, they wrestle to hold onto their friendship. Written and directed by acclaimed artist Imran Perretta and co-written by Enda Walsh ( Hunger ), Ish was shot in black and white by cinematographer Jermaine Canute Edwards ( My Father’s Shadow ). The film is less contemporary urban drama and more a classical coming-of-age story in the tradition of The Apu Trilogy , Kes and Ratcatcher .

https://www.ica.art/films/the-last-one-f.description: Surviving bar-to-bar on anecdotes and the ‘good old days’, two blustery 50-somethings hatch a plan to change their luck by digging up the cash their old pal buried before he left for Argentina. En route to the airport, they come across a shy architecture student whose view of life will transform as they take him under their wing on a road trip across the Venetian plains. Francesco Sossai’s dazzling sophomore feature is many things at once: a road movie, a casual caper, a tribute to a vanishing industrial Italy, a scruffy intergenerational odyssey, and free-flowing bender through time and space.

https://www.ica.art/films/oshima-the-cat.description: During the final days of World War II, a remote village community is shaken by the capture of an African-American pilot. As they figure out what to do with him, tensions flare between the village headman and other inhabitants, bringing long-repressed resentments to the surface. Made on the heels of his angry break with Shochiku over their unyielding suppression of Night and Fog in Japan, Ōshima delivers a categorical rejection of the humanistic interpretations of the war prevalent in postwar Japanese cinema.

https://www.ica.art/films/personal-probl.description: A legendary meta-soap opera that has maintained a devoted underground following since 1981, it captures the improvisational heat of Harlem life on gritty U-matic video to explore what Ishmael Reed calls the "triteness of everyday life."

https://www.ica.art/films/memory.description: Six-year-old Vladlena moves from Crimea to Grozny following her parents' divorce, unaware that war will soon consume her childhood. As the Soviet Union collapses, the Chechen Republic fractures. Her Russian-speaking friends flee while deported Chechens return, reclaiming their homeland. Tensions escalate, and an armed conflict erupts. Violence engulfs the city - neighbours are murdered, her family is targeted, and Grozny becomes a battlefield. After four years of war, her mother is gravely wounded, and an armed attack forces Vladlena to flee, becoming a displaced person in Russia. In this autobiographical poetic hybrid film, Vladlena revisits her traumatic childhood memories to confront a haunting question: How can the cycle of violence that shapes children and is passed through generations be broken?

https://www.ica.art/films/off-circuit-th.description: 30-year-old Danielius returns to his hometown to sell his parents’ flat, but the visit lasts longer than expected. With nowhere to rush, he tries to reconnect with the people and the town that no longer feels like his. Vytautas Katkus' debut feature is a delicate study of homecoming, fatherhood, and belated farewells.

https://www.ica.art/films/pin-de-fartie.description: The latest production from boundlessly imaginative Argentine collective El Pampero Cine sees successive pairs of characters bid farewell: a mother and her son, a caretaker and her charge, two actors endlessly rehearsing a scene that will never be performed. A playful spin on theatrical adaptation, Alejo Moguillansky's new film is a delightfully imaginative take on Samuel Beckett's Fin de Partie , punctuated by music, tennis, and another exceptional turn by Laura Paredes. The UK Premiere screening on the 4 September will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Alejo Moguillansky.

https://www.ica.art/films/soldier-girls-.description: Contemporary Films 75th Anniversary Nick Broomfield and Joan Churchill’s riveting documentary, shot over 3 months, following a group of women going through basic training for the US Army. Fifty started out but only thirty made it through to the end. They concentrate on three of the young women: an 18-year old black woman whose constant giggling and grins drive the platoon sergeant to distraction, another who provides encouragement and support to the others who find it hard, and a third woman who also finds she cannot tolerate army life but is more inhibited. You see each of them change as they face the challenges and rigours before them, all captured with startling intimacy by Broomfield and Churchill. As Broomfield states on his own website: “Joan and I went through Basic Training for 14 weeks. Fred Wiseman lent us a tape recorder. [D.A.] Pennebaker and Chris Hegedus lent us a cutting room. We only got funding after it was shot. We both lost 20 pounds making it – it was so hot.” After the screening directors Nick Broomfield (in person) and Joan Churchill (via live Zoom), will discuss the film.

https://www.ica.art/films/off-circuit-th.description: Weaving accounts of rural workers and field notes of a couple of archaeologists, amateur footage and scientific drawings, legends, poems and songs, Maureen Fazendeiro's The Seasons is a journey through the real history and the tales of a region in southern Portugal, Alentejo, and a portrait of the people who have lived there.

https://www.ica.art/films/cf75-blanche.description: Contemporary Films 75th Anniversary Walerian Borowczyk’s critically acclaimed and influential medieval tale — a beautiful tragedy told with pitch-black humour and the director’s remarkable idiosyncratic inventiveness. Arguably Borowczyk’s most ambitious film, a meticulous recreation of medieval life by way of references from the history of art, not least Giotto’s religious paintings. Occupying the space between Pasolini and Parajanov as a sort of flat, two-dimensional moving tapestry, Blanche is based on a drama by the great Polish romantic poet Juliusz Słowacki, Mazepa. Featuring one of the last performances by the Swiss actor Michel Simon, not to mention a spirited turn by the late Jacques Perrin (also serving as an uncredited producing partner here), Blanche herself is played by Ligia Branice as a Sadean stock character whose innocent gothic beauty evokes male lust inevitably followed by bloody violence. While Borowczyk was able to realize his medieval masterpiece with complete artistic control, Blanche was a critical if not commercial success in France, but fared much better during Contemporary’s British run where it played for 20 weeks at Contemporary’s Paris Pullman cinema alone. Enthusiasts included documentary filmmaker Leslie Megahey, whose own Schalcken the Painter (1979) it influenced, Monty Python’s Terry Jones and Terry Gilliam (the latter cited the film, along with Pasolini, as key references when conjuring the medieval onscreen in Monty Python and the Holy Grail and Jabberwocky ), and the novelist and critic Marina Warner, who included Blanche in her study of fairy tales From the Beast to the Blonde . More than half a century later, two aspects of the film remain particularly striking: the way Borowczyk creates a flat, face-on world, like an animated tapestry, and its soundtrack, which set out to reconstruct the sound of authentic 13th-century musical instruments. The screening will be introduced by Daniel Bird, Co-founder of Friends of Walerian Borowczyk , a non-profit association based in Paris that manages the rights to the painter, sculptor and filmmaker. He will discuss Borowczyk’s association with Contemporary, and will be joined by Kathleen Wallfisch, Music Supervisor for film and TV, to talk about the music of the film and how it is arranged and presented on screen.

https://www.ica.art/films/tape-collectiv.description: Wrestling with writer’s block for her first film, Bouchra, a queer Moroccan jackal living in NYC, starts having difficult yet overdue phone calls with her mother in Casablanca that begin influencing the project. Balancing the precarity of working as an artist in New York, the rift in her identity between her two homes and an array of friendships and romantic interests, Bouchra’s emotional reckoning with her mother and herself becomes her path to expression.

https://www.ica.art/films/songs-of-forgo.description: Thooya, a migrant and aspiring actress, secretly works as a part time sex worker in Mumbai. When she sublets her sugar daddy’s flat to Swetha, a call-centre employee and a migrant, an unexpected connection begins to form. Their lives, seemingly worlds apart, slowly entangle. Amid the city’s chaos, they share silences, stories, and small acts of care. But as buried desires and past wounds emerge, the fragile bond is tested. What unfolds is not drama, but a quiet blooming of selfhood, survival, and strange and platonic kinship between women navigating a world that rarely sees them.

https://www.ica.art/films/oshima-death-b.description: The botched execution of a Korean citizen convicted of rape and murder brings the judiciary system to a halt, as wardens, prosecutors, medics, and even the clergy discuss whether a man who survived his execution can be executed a second time. At one disturbing and oddly amusing, Ōshima's macabre farce is a searing indictment of both capital punishment and the treatment of Korean immigrants in his country. Preceded by Ōshima's experimental documentary from 1965 Yunbogi's Diary .

https://www.ica.art/films/oshima-diary-o.description: When a thief is caught stealing form a book shop by one of its employees, the two embark on an unusual, erotic adventure. Set against the vivid backdrop of the massive student-led riots, Nagisa Ōshima's radical concoction of cinema verité, underground kabuki and just about everything in-between is a striking meditation on the psychosexual ambiguities of the postwar counterculture.

https://www.ica.art/films/tfff-drinking-.description: Early twenties Iris and Palmer never left their hometown. They work at the same restaurant, share the same bed, and both have a habit of drinking and driving.They run into Levi, a guy they used to know. They spend time with him and his cousin, Phoenix, in cars, backyards, and other people’s bedrooms. When Levi shares a dream he had with Iris things change between the four of them. The reality of the summer becomes faded, the parties die. The four end in a field of unified confusion. Drinking and Driving is something of a miracle movie. Frank and Fast work against conventional ideas of craft, embracing limitation as formal strategy and cinematic ingenuity. The film carries the aura of sweaty summer days, intoxicated with friends, suspended in the hope of fleeting intimacy. What begins as euphoria gradually gives way to a very specific kind of summertime ennui, evoking deeply personal memories that feel both specific and strangely universal, where experience itself becomes blurred and half-remembered. Nonetheless it resists the charm of sentimentality; instead, memory is rendered as something unstable, closer to a dream you can’t quite translate into language. Since its premiere at LAFM in April, Drinking and Driving has begun to develop a cult following and establishes its writers, directors (and stars) as two of the most exciting emerging filmmakers working today. A nauseating, disoriented debut of real formal confidence, the film announces a filmmaking partnership not to be missed.

https://www.ica.art/films/tfff-pola-x.description: Pierre is a successful young author enjoying a life of bourgeois comfort whilst he works on his latest novel. All of this will change upon the arrival of a young woman claiming to be his long-lost sister. Bewitched by her, the two run away to the city where they will be met with desperation, poverty and nihilistic self-destruction as their relationship blooms. Controversial upon initial release, Pola X is the fifth feature film from acclaimed filmmaker Leos Carax. Seeking a change in tone and style from his previous works, he went about adapting Herman Melville's novel Pierre, or The Ambiguities , situating it in contemporary France against the wider milieu of Europe in the 1990s. Darker and more explicit than earlier works, Pola X failed to gain the same cult reputation as his more broadly acclaimed titles and as such has fallen by the wayside in terms of evaluation, being seen as neither in-step with the initial run nor associated with his resurgence in feature filmmaking 13 years later. As a result, Pola X has languished in obscurity, without even so much as a high definition home entertainment release for now. Fortunately, this screening will be vividly restoring the murky, oblique imagery of this under-appreciated work for the first time in the UK and it's an honour to be showing it as part of The Final Film Festival.

https://www.ica.art/films/jukebox-film-c.description: Armenian Film Society London presents the UK premiere of In the Land of Arto (2025), the debut fiction by Tamara Stepanyan, as part of Jukebox Film Club. Céline travels to Armenia in search of traces of her recently deceased husband, Arto. When no record of him can be found in the archives, she sets out on a journey through a land scarred by war. Along the way, the truth gradually emerges through the testimonies of Arto’s former fellow soldiers: the memory of a deserter who jeopardised his own combat unit before assuming a new identity to flee Armenia during the Nagorno-Karabakh war of the 1990s. But did she ever really know her husband at all? The past year has been especially fruitful for French-Armenian filmmaker Tamara Stepanyan. Her documentary essay My Armenian Phantoms (2025) premiered in the Forum section of the Berlin International Film Festival, while In the Land of Arto opened the prestigious Locarno Film Festival at the Piazza Grande. The former received its UK premiere at the Armenian Film Festival London, while the latter arrives at the Institute of Contemporary Arts this September. In the Land of Arto uses the structure of a travelogue to confront the painful legacy of the Nagorno-Karabakh wars, a conflict that continues to overshadow the modern history of Armenia and echoes the unresolved trauma of the early-20th-century Armenian Genocide. Framed as a road movie, the film follows two women — one French, the other Armenian, though portrayed by a French-Iranian actress — as they journey across the Armenian Highlands in search of the roots of tragedy, betrayal, and displaced identity. The screening is organised in collaboration with Iranian Film Club and will be followed by an in-person Q&A with the filmmaker hosted by Kira Adibekov (AFSL).

https://www.ica.art/films/tfff-a-rimbaud.description: The improbable life of French poet Arthur Rimbaud unfolds with all the shock and playfulness of his poetry.

https://www.ica.art/films/i-want-your-se.description: Gregg Araki's I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twentysomething whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries, and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli XCX) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery, and murder through the colourful and edgy visual language for which Araki is best known.

https://www.ica.art/films/late-fame.description: Willem Defoe plays Ed Saxberger, a forgotten New York poet, who works in the post office. After an eager and flattering young admirer appears on his doorstep, Saxberger is beckoned into a coterie of twentysomething admirers who anoint him as a rediscovered genius. Intoxicated by the attention — and by the alluring presence of Gloria, the group’s “tragic heroine” — Saxberger gradually reckons with the authenticity of his newfound poetic circle. Kent Jones's thoughtful, witty film is a wistful yet unromantic look at a lost idea of downtown New York.

https://www.ica.art/films/picture-this-q.description: Directed by Anna Fox, Sarah Jeans and Anne Parisio, Picture This is a heartwarming portrait of three groups of women in Edinburgh, Farnham and London. The women are from refugee and migrant communities and a women’s refuge, as they have all had to leave their own countries or homes because of war, their sexuality or to escape abusive relationships. Professor Anna Fox, an internationally renowned photographer and university lecturer introduces us to the different participants as they receive training to use photography to reinterpret their experiences and create moving images. Through a series of industry visits, industry partners and visiting lectures, Anna introduces the women to aspects of the industry with the aim of helping them to develop future careers in the photography industries. Picture This , is an output of Putting Ourselves in The Picture – Part 2 Engaging With Industry which has been funded through the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) and the University for The Creative Arts (UCA). The project is part of Fast Forward: Women in Photography, which was established in 2014 at UCA Farnham, UK. Fast Forward is a world wide research network that gathers and disseminates new knowledge about past and present female photographers, with the aim of empowering women through engaging in debate, discourse and dissemination about these often hidden histories. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the directors and participants.

https://www.ica.art/films/ghost-town.description: In a Japanese coastal town still haunted by the 2011 tsunami, a taxi becomes a moving confession booth. Over the course of one night, a series of conversations between drivers and their passengers reveal how those who survived live with the dead – as ghostly tales, dreams and everyday life merge in a magical drift between reality and imagination. The screening at the ICA on Tuesday 27 October is the London Premiere of Ghost Town .

https://www.ica.art/films/oshima-boy.description: When a man crippled during the war remarries, he and his new bride each bring a child from their previous relationship. Unable to hold a normal job, the father forces his family to participate in fake hit-and-run incidents, to extort money from the unwitting drivers. Based on a shocking true story and making brilliant use of its widescreen cinematography, Boy is one of Ōshima's most beautiful and restrained films.

https://www.ica.art/films/oshima-the-man.description: A young filmmaker intent on committing suicide captures his final days on film, but after the young man's death the footage is seized by the police. As his comrades discuss ways to get hold of the film and camera, the most radical among them decides to take matters into his own hands. One of the most urgent, anxious cinematic interventions into the post-1968 defeat of the radical youth movement, Ōshima's The Man Who Left His Will on Film is anchored by its feverish and lingering enigma, one that has lost none of its power to captivate nearly sixty years on from the films first release.

https://www.ica.art/films/a-rimbaud.description: The improbable life of French poet Arthur Rimbaud unfolds with all the shock and playfulness of his poetry.

https://www.ica.art/films/kiki-s-deliver.description: Celebrate this beloved coming-of-age story from the legendary Studio Ghibli, creators of Spirited Away , and Academy Award®-winning director Hayao Miyazaki, about a resourceful young witch who uses her broom to create a delivery service, only to lose her gift of flight in a moment of self-doubt. It is a tradition for all young witches to leave their families on the night of a full moon and fly off into the wide world to learn their craft. When that night comes for Kiki, she embarks on her new journey with her sarcastic black cat, Jiji, landing the next morning in a seaside town, where her unique skills make her an instant sensation.

https://www.ica.art/films/matador.description: Pedro Almodóvar's 1986 erotic thriller explores the intimate relationship between pleasure and death through the convergence of bullfighting and murder. Diego is an ex-champion matador who now runs a bullfighting school. Still looking for a kick, he watches sadistic videos for sexual pleasure. Maria is a lawyer and Diego’s number one fan – she also likes to kill men with a hairpin at the point of orgasm. The pair are destined to meet.

https://www.ica.art/films/sherman-s-marc.description: Sherman’s March , winner of the Grand Jury Prize for Best Documentary at Sundance in 1987, is Ross McElwee’s monumental documentary which has been officially listed by the International Documentary Association as one of the top 20 documentary films of all time. Intending to make a film about General Sherman’s 1864 March to the Sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. Affected by a recent breakup, he slows his progress through the American South to spend time with a succession of women and explore the possibility of romantic fulfilment in the nuclear age.

https://www.ica.art/films/remake.description: In Remake , filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, Sherman’s March . What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

https://www.ica.art/films/sonic-cinema-d.description: Sonic Cinema and the Japan Foundation present the films of Montreal-based artist Daïchi Saïto, projected from his personal 35mm prints. A rare encounter with a singular voice in artisanal film practice, this programme highlights Saïto’s skill in bridging metaphysical concepts with sensory experience. Originally from Japan, Daïchi Saïto makes films of intense beauty and power, grounded in abstract approaches to landscape, rhythm, and perception. Produced through expressive use of optical manipulation and painstaking frame-by-frame photochemical treatments, the films in this programme carry a tactile and elemental intensity, teasing out the sensual poetry of the natural world and human subjectivity. Drawing on Saïto's studies in philosophy, literature, and the languages of Hindi and Sanskrit, as much as the language of cinema, these are films built on a poetic dialogue of sound and image. Guided by the expressive improvised soundtracks of Malcolm Goldstein and Jason Sharp, we'll traverse exterior and interior landscapes, from the darkened primordial deserts of Saïto's most recent film earthearthearth (2021), through the stained glass forest of Trees of Syntax , Leaves of Axis (2009), before the torrent of memories and cool mountain vistas carries us away in Engram of Returning (2015). Daïchi will join us in person for a Q&A with series curator Oliver Dickens following the screening. Programme earthearthearth , Canada 2021, 30 min., 35mm Trees of Syntax, Leaves of Axis , Canada 2009, 10 min., 35mm Engram of Returning , Canada, Japan 2015, 18’30 min., 35mm Programmed by Oliver Dickens for Sonic Cinema, presented in partnership with the Japan Foundation.

https://www.ica.art/films/a-free-woman.description: On the cusp of marriage, Liana becomes convinced she shouldn't live a life in service of a man. Instead, she leaves for Amalfi, where she embarks on an affair. From there she makes for Paris, but each new adventure is compromised by some kind of emotional constraint, culminating in a final act of tragedy. Vittorio Cottafavi's remarkably modern exploration of female autonomy exhibits the melodramatic finesse of Douglas Sirk with a style reminiscent of Max Ophuls. A Free Woman has been newly restored by Radiance.

https://www.ica.art/films/manhunter-4k-r.description: In celebration of the 40th anniversary of Michael Mann’s Manhunter , Mann’s final cut of the film returns in a newly restored 4K version. FBI criminal profiler Will Graham is called out of early retirement to assist on a deadly case involving a murderer known as the “Tooth Fairy.” After enlisting the help of imprisoned serial killer Dr. Hannibal Lecktor, Graham and the FBI are soon entangled in a menacing cat-and-mouse game.

https://www.ica.art/films/edges-of-cinem.description: Join us to celebrate the publication of Erika Balsom's The Edges of Cinema: Essays on Twenty-First Century Film Culture with the London premiere of James Benning's little boy (2025). Recent years have seen a panic over the future of mainstream film. Yet in her new collection The Edges of Cinema , Balsom argues that film culture is at its most vital on the margins, where the moving image meets visual art, documentary brushes up against experimentalism, and curators are reshaping established histories. Bringing together a decade of selected essays and reviews, the book explores subjects ranging from computer-generated animation to the effects of digitisation, and from the status of observational cinema to a new golden age of repertory cinema, in order to make a case for the politics, provocations, and pleasures of a less ordinary cinema. To celebrate this publication, join us for the first London screening of little boy by James Benning, an artist and filmmaker central to the book. For some fifty years, Benning has chronicled American hegemony and counterhegemony through an expert manipulation of light and time, giving unconventional shape to histories of settlement, racial violence, land use, and unbelonging. In little boy – winner of the grand prize at Paris's Cinéma du Réel festival – he continues this investigation, using popular songs, political speeches, and architectural models to traverse decades of U.S. history. What are the rules governing the organisation of all these component parts? That is left for the viewer to discern. In Benning's words, little boy is "a film looking at the past to warn about the future, from a little boy’s point of view. A companion to American Dreams (lost and found) (1984).”

https://www.ica.art/films/queen-at-sea.description: Starring Juliette Binoche, Tom Courtenay and Anna Calder-Marshall, Queen at Sea received its world premiere in competition at the Berlin International Film Festival earlier this year, where it won both the Silver Bear Jury Prize and the Silver Bear for Best Supporting Performance for both Courtenay and Calder-Marshall. The film follows Amanda (Binoche) and her stepfather, Martin (Courtney), at odds over a moral quandary involving Amanda’s mother, Leslie (Calder-Marshall). In the advanced stages of dementia, they quarrel over whether Leslie has lost all ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests, and, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

https://www.ica.art/films/listen-with-yo.description: Listen with your eyes is an ongoing series of screenings for children of all ages and their grown-up companions. It’s a space where curious minds and open hearts can come together to drift through the worlds of experimental cinema. Shown on 16mm and 35mm, the films in this programme span a period of 70 years, from the hand-painted and stencilled imagery of Len Lye ( Colour Flight , 1938), to the stroboscopic study on the history of weaving patterns of Jodie Mack ( Persian Pickles , 2012). Showcasing a large variety of techniques (painting, animation, flicker, etc.), the programme is also a journey through vastly different worlds, ranging from the magical realm invented by Anita Thacher ( Loose Corner , 1986) to the cosmogonic trip created by J.A. Sistiaga ( Impressions en haute atmosphère , 1989), and taking in uncanny observations of the animal world (R. Breer, G. Rey, and J. Smith) along the way. All the films are selected from the collection of Light Cone, a non-profit distributor of experimental films based in Paris, among the 7,500 films of their catalogue. Ticket holders are welcome to join us early for a free 16mm direct animation activity between 10am and 11am. Please note that this is a relaxed screening, open to children of all ages. Programme : Abstronic Mary Ellen Bute & Ted Nemeth I 1952 I Digital I colour I sound I 6 min "Beautiful Lissajous, curves can be put through a choreography that inspires – and startles – the imagination." – Mary Ellen Bute Bread Deborah Phillips I 1994 I 16mm I colour I sound I 3 min Loosely based on Lewis Caroll's Through the Looking Glass , Bread is a series of metamorphoses. Colour Flight Len Lye I 1938 I 16mm I colour I sound I 4 min This film is a riot of colour and a showcase for Lye’s hand-painted and stencilled imagery. Gargantuan John Smith I 1992 I 16mm I colour I sound I 1 min "A wonderful and witty example of what it can be to have a pillowtalk with a small amphibian." – Elaine Paterson Impressions en haute atmosphère José Antonio Sistiaga I 1989 I 35mm I colour I sound I 7 min "The colours don't appear randomly but elaborate a logic of dynamics, continual movement of energy-matter." – Claira Janes Loose Corner Anitha Thacher I 1986 I 16mm I colour I sound I 10 min In the film we accompany a man and a woman, a child and a dog, as well as objects, to an impossible place: a corner (...) The surprises in the corner... surprise and satisfy us too. A Man and His Dog Out For Air Robert Breer I 1957 I 16mm I b&w I sound I 3 min "I can describe [the film] as a stew: something recognisable comes to the surface and disappears immediately." – Robert Breer Persian Pickles Jodie Mack I 2012 I 16mm I colour I sound I 2 min A swimming study of paisley patterns traces this decorative motif from its origins in Persian weavings to appearances in Irish quilting and American Counterculture. La vache qui rumine George Rey I 1969 / 16mm I b&w I silent I 3 min First she cows, then she cows. Standing shot of a cowing cow which plays with the filmmaker and so with the audience.

https://www.ica.art/films/arrows-of-desi.description: To celebrate the publication of a new anthology of Peter Wollen's texts, Arrows of Desire: Selected Writings 1963–2002 , there will be a screening of his solo feature film Friendship’s Death (1987) and a conversation with the book's editors, Kodwo Eshun, Oliver Fuke and Nicolas Helm-Grovas. There will be a short reception with books available for purchase at 7pm. The conversation with the book’s editors will take place in the cinema at 8.30pm. Arrows of Desire , the first of three new volumes, brings together unpublished and inaccessible writings on counter-cinema, anti-imperialist politics and revolutionary Mexican art. Playful, theoretically rigorous and historically precise, Wollen’s writing reinvented criticism as a formally experimental practice indexing the intellectual, political and artistic histories of the twentieth century. The book presents texts on Eisenstein and Godard alongside essays and interviews tracing developments in film and video from the 1970s to the 1990s. It tracks the political energies running through Wollen’s filmmaking and writing on global politics and culture in relation to Iran, Indonesia, Palestine, Aden and Zanzibar. It also presents texts relating to Wollen’s film, Friendship’s Death , adapted from his science fiction story, published in Bananas, Emma Tennant’s literary magazine, in 1976. Starring Tilda Swinton as an alien android from Procyon, who lands in Amman, Jordan, days before the events sometimes referred to as ‘Black September’, the film and short story are, in part, informed by Wollen’s experience as a political journalist, writing on global politics for New Left Review and International Socialist Journal. The texts presented in Arrows of Desire illuminate the film and testify to Wollen’s enduring commitment to anti-imperialist politics.

https://www.ica.art/films/everybody-digs.description: Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival, Everybody Digs Bill Evans is a biographical drama film about the famous jazz pianist and composer Bill Evans. In 1961, Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro – his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface. The screening on Friday 11th September will be followed by a Q&A with director Grant Gee and actor Valene Kane

https://www.ica.art/films/her-private-he.description: From filmmaker Nicolas Winding Refn ( Drive , Only God Forgives , The Neon Demon ), Her Private Hell is a hypnotic moodscape enshrined in pink mist. Set against a surrealist, futuristic metropolis, the story follows Elle (Sophie Thatcher), a rising movie star preparing to shoot a space odyssey alongside her ex-lover turned stepmother (Havana Rose Liu). Elsewhere in the haze, an American GI (Charles Melton) wanders the desolate streets on a desperate search for his daughter. As an enigmatic and sinister figure known only as the Leather Man stalks the city's shadows, their lives begin to converge, dissolving the boundaries between past and present, memory and fate. Driven by his trademark neon cinematography, striking atmospheric dread, and an intoxicating orchestral score by legendary composer Pino Donaggio, Her Private Hell is a breathtaking, kaleidoscopic experience designed to mesmerise and seduce.

https://www.ica.art/films/barrio-triste.description: In an impoverished neighborhood of 1980s Medellín, a group of disaffected teens steal a TV reporter’s camera to document their lives. Piercing the derelict landscape’s oppressive atmosphere with disarming reflections on dreams and death, their understanding of reality and hope begins to erode as reports of mysterious lights falling from the sky coincide with temporal and spatial distortions. In his striking feature debut, long-time Bad Bunny collaborator Stillz captures an intimate, formally daring portrait of Colombia's forgotten youth. Barrio Triste is heightened by a restless, intense debut score from Arca, whose fluid soundscapes anchor the film's vision. Navigating the thin line between desperation and the supernatural, Stillz delivers a beautiful, unclassifiable piece of contemporary cinema.

https://www.ica.art/films/nadja.description: In 1993, invited by David Lynch to come up with a low-budget genre movie, Michael Almereyda ( Tesla , Experimenter , Hamlet ) came up with a moody, postmodern reimagining of the Dracula myth which draws inspiration from Dracula’s Daughter (1936) and André Breton’s surrealist novel Nadja . The film follows estranged vampire twins Nadja (Elina Löwensohn) and Edgar (a young Jared Harris) as they reunite following their father’s death by the flamboyantly unhinged Dr. Van Helsing, played with relish by Peter Fonda. The film’s striking visuals combine high-contrast black-and-white 35mm cinematography with the hallucinatory grain of Pixelvision video is now newly restored in 4K.

https://www.ica.art/films/case-137.description: Set against the backdrop of mass protests in Paris, Case 137 follows Stéphanie, a meticulous internal affairs investigator working on the case of a teenager severely wounded by police fire. As she searches for the truth her inquiry collides with institutional resistance and pressure mounts as the case takes a personal turn when she discovers the victim is from her hometown.

https://www.ica.art/films/by-design.description: Upon seeing a gorgeous chair in a showroom, Camille (Juliette Lewis) realises that she truly envies the life of this perfect piece of furniture. If only she could be someone’s favourite thing. When she and the chair swap forms, Camille learns that she is better liked as an inanimate object than she was as a person: her mother (Betty Buckley) finds her to be a better listener, and her best friends (Samantha Mathis and Robin Tunney) enjoy a newfound, friction-free rapport. As the chair, Camille is unable to speak or move and winds up in the hands of Olivier (Mamoudou Athie), a minimalist bachelor who gradually becomes romantically fixated on his elegant new possession. Narrated by Melanie Griffith, this modern fable celebrates the messiness of female interiority with deadpan humour, surrealist flourishes, and interpretative dance numbers. An absurdist spin on the body-swap comedy, By Design is a bold new work from singular filmmaker Amanda Kramer.

https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-the-aviat.description: Hong Kong Film Festival UK 2026 Twenty-year-old François (Philippe Marlaud) is madly in love with his girlfriend Anne (Marie Rivière), five years his senior. One morning, he spots her leaving her apartment with married pilot Christian (Mathieu Carrière). Swelling with jealousy and all kinds of speculation, he decides to tail the man across Paris – an impulsive pursuit that leads him to Lucie (Anne-Laure Meury), a vivacious teenage girl who is intrigued by his odd behaviour and ends up joining his investigation. Mary Stephen first met Éric Rohmer as a student on his course. They began their creative collaboration on The Aviator's Wife , with Stephen working as assistant editor to Cécile Decugis, who also edited several landmark films from the French New Wave, including Jean-Luc Godard’s Breathless . Stephen also made a brief appearance in the film. Followed by an in-person Q&A with Mary Stephen. Presented as a collaboration between Hong Kong Film Festival UK and the ICA.

https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-a-summer-.description: Hong Kong Film Festival UK 2026 Gaspard (Melvil Poupaud), a math graduate and musician, arrives in Dinard, a seaside town in Brittany, awaiting his girlfriend Lena (Aurélia Nolin) for the summer holiday. As the wait drags on indefinitely, he has romantic encounters with two charming women: Margot (Amanda Langlet), an aspiring ethnographer who works at a restaurant, and her friend Solène (Gwenaëlle Simon). Gaspard’s indecisiveness about who to pursue leaves his chances at love hanging in the balance. A Tale of Summer is the third installment of Éric Rohmer’s Tales of the Four Seasons series and, according to the filmmaker himself, the most autobiographical of his work. Mary Stephen not only collaborated with Rohmer on the film as an editor, but also worked with him on the music under the pseudonym ‘Sébastien Erms’, creating the melodious sea shanty the protagonist wrote in the film. Followed by an in-person Q&A with Mary Stephen. Presented as a collaboration between Hong Kong Film Festival UK and the ICA.

https://www.ica.art/films/bodies-adrift-.description: The second programme of Bodies Adrift traces the Villaverde filmmaking couple trajectory from revolutionary Cuba in the early 1960s to the experimental underground scene of 1970s New York. Beginning with The Park (1963), filmed in one of Havana’s epicentres, and continuing through a series of intimate works made in exile, the session reveals their continuous reinvention of cinematic form and production methods. Moving from institutional filmmaking to a radically independent practice shot on 16mm with minimal resources, the Villaverdes remained at the margins of the cultural movements they inhabited. Their Cuban films were often censored or scarcely exhibited, while their US output has only recently begun to be discovered through restorations by the Filmoteca de Catalunya. Across these films runs a persistent attention to lives situated at the edges of societal structures: the elderly figures wandering through The Park ; immigrants navigating displacement ( A Lady’s Home Journal , 1972); and women confronting domestic roles and gender violence ( Blanca Putica , 1973; Poor Cinderella , 1978). As the filmmakers moved from Cuba to the United States, their cinema shifted from observing bodies in public space to examining their own within the private confines of home. The result is a body of work that quietly resists grand historical narratives in favour of the fragile, everyday experiences of those who remain on the margins. Programme El parque ( The Park ) dir. Fernando Villaverde, Cuba 1963, 25 min. Blanca Putica ( A Girl in Love ) dir. Miñuca Villaverde, USA/Cuba 1973, 14 min. Poor Cinderella, Still Ironing Her Husband Shirt dir. Miñuca Villaverde, USA 1978, 7 min. A Lady’s Home Journal dir. Fernando Villaverde, Miñuca Villaverde, USA 1972, 20 min. Total runtime: 67 min.

https://www.ica.art/films/cotton-queen.description: In a cotton-farming village in Sudan, teenage Nafisa is raised on heroic tales of battling British colonisers told by her grandmother, the village matriarch Al-Sit. But when a young businessman arrives from abroad with a new development plan and genetically engineered cotton, Nafisa becomes the centre of a power play to determine the future of the village. Awakening to her own strength, Nafisa sets out to save the cotton fields – and herself. Neither she nor her community will ever be the same again.

https://www.ica.art/films/fatherland.description: The new offering from Oscar-winner Pawel Pawlikowski Fatherland centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

https://www.ica.art/films/possible-love.description: Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. Marking his first release in eight years, highly acclaimed director Lee Chang-dong ( Burning , Poetry , Secret Sunshine ) brings his signature nuance to Possible Love , capturing shifting emotions, conflicts, and contrasting outlooks that shape these relationships.

https://www.ica.art/films/andy-warhol-s-.description: Éditions 1989 celebrates the launch of the second edition of Who Are You Dorothy Dean? When Dorothy Dean (1932–1987) entered the 1960s New York underground scene, she quickly became one of its key figures, starring in six of Andy Warhol's films and inspiring the likes of Robert Mapplethorpe and Robert Creeley. Said to be the first woman ever hired as a fact-checker at The New Yorker , Dean held brief editorial and proofreading positions at publications such as Vogue before launching her very own bulletin of film reviews, the All-Lavender Cinema Courier , in 1976. But in histories of the era, she has often been overlooked. The evening will feature a special 40-minute excerpt from Andy Warhol's Prison (1965), inspired by Bibbe Hansen's experiences in a juvenile detention centre and featuring Dean. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with author Anaïs Ngbanzo, moderated by Róisín Tapponi. Books will be available for purchase and signing.

https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-i-heard-t.description: Tao (Elizabeth Tang) is infatuated with Shin (Shin Cheung) and trying to invent a way to make their relationship leave an indelible mark on him — and the idea she lands on is to inflict pain, like sending gangs to beat him up on the street. Melih (Melih Selçuk), the Turkish owner of a noodle shop the couple frequents, is also struggling to connect with someone he’s in love with: Ping (Wang Yu-ping), who one day sent him a flower out of the blue. As Melih stares at the flower day after day, he gains an unexpected insight into Tao’s story, and the two develop an inexplicable connection with each other. Playful, quirky, and poetic, Ka Ki Wong’s first feature transforms the streets of Taipei into a kaleidoscopic lucid dream, probing the relationship between connection, memory, and pain through the intertwined stories of her characters, whom the filmmaker interviews, leaving us unsure whether the answers are coming from the actors themselves or from the characters they play. Followed by an in-person Q&A with Ka Ki Wong, moderated by Erin Li, Curator (Public Programmes and Residencies) at YDP. English subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing (SDH). British Sign Language (BSL) interpretation provided for post-screening discussion.

https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-inherited.description: Across generations, migration takes many forms: the quiet rooting of a plant, the courage to leave and return, the written word as a thread that binds people across distance and separation. This programme traces experiences of migration across different times and places – people who arrived in Hong Kong, and those who later left it for the UK – allowing conversations around home and identity to unfold from narrative cinema into documentary and artist moving images. Beginning with the perspectives of women filmmakers, we move across borders and geographies, following the ways in which people leave, return, adapt, and take root again. Followed by in-person discussion with the filmmakers. Programme The First Photograph 第一張照片 Hong Kong | 2024 | Colour | 11’ | No Dialogue with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Jess Lau Ching-wa 劉清華 UK Premiere The film depicts the story of the artist's father, who fled to Hong Kong in the 70s. The video is presented in a series of overlays and montages, initially taken from one of her father's documentary photographs, and then combined with Google Maps to retrace the route of his escape from China, as well as newspaper articles and radio broadcasts from 1978 to 1980. as a bird that briefly perches Hong Kong, UK | 2024/2025 | Colour | 17’ | In Cantonese with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Dorothy Cheung 張紫茵 A cinematic diary weaves Hong Kong's geology, greenhouse gardening, and UK migrant farmers' lives, exploring rooting, re-rooting, and growing amid shifting land-human dynamics. Homecoming and Going 逆留 Hong Kong, UK | 2025 | Colour | 19’ | In Cantonese and English with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Kristie Ko 高思約 An apartment is handed over between old friends. It is Emily and Vincent’s first day in London, and Megan’s last day before returning to Hong Kong. As Emily and Vincent start their new life, Megan bids farewell to the people and places she has grown to call home. Heart of the Lion 赤子獅心 Hong Kong, UK | 2026 | Colour | 20’ | In English with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Rosanna Lee 李學儀 Moving between life in London and Hong Kong, this film follows Kelvin Chan, a British-born Chinese lion dancer, as he explores how the routines and rituals of a creative, spiritual practice may provide their own sense of belonging. Tiger’s Head, Nail’s Tail: Yours Faithfully Hong Kong, Thailand, Netherlands | 2025 | Colour | 28’ | No Dialogue with English subtitles Dir.: Serene Hui 許思樂 UK Premiere The essay-film is a montage of conversations with Hui's grandfather, archival material and footage from migration sites, centred on his role as scribe within Qiaopi – a vital 20th-century correspondence and remittance network for the Chinese diaspora. It explores trust and time involved in historical letter transmission versus contemporary communication, reframing transcribing to illuminate a momentous displacement's emotional and political contours.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-memory-.description: This programme brings together five short films exploring themes of memory, family, return and identity. Across different generations and relationships between parents and children, the films reflect on what is passed down to us and what we inherit – memories, stories, identities and experiences. They move between being away from home and returning to it, often confronting memories that are complex, fragmented or difficult, and asking how these shape our sense of who we are and where we belong. Programme Start Coming Back ( Empezar a volver ) dir. David Ovanco Torres, Chile 2025 Astronaut ( Astronauta ) dir. Giorgio Giampà, France, Guatemala, Mexico 2025 I don’t know if I'll have to say everything again , dir. Vitória Fallavena & Thassilo Weber, Brazil 2024 Finding Pá, dir. Enrique Lebron, USA 2025 Pasta Negra, dir. Jorge Thielen Armand, Canada, Venezuela, Italy, Colombia 2025 Total runtime: 86 min.

https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-i-m-fine-.director: Kanas Liu 廖潔雯 and Sui-Ting Kong 江瑞婷
https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-i-m-fine-.description: I am fine, thank you. documents the stories of Hongkongers who migrated to the UK after 2019, as each gradually settled into a new life in the country while finding their own way to connect with memories of the homeland. How are you? A simple greeting can often be the most difficult question to answer — if you take it seriously enough, and if the person asking cares enough to learn the details. For many Hongkongers, it is easiest to spare the details: the complicated experience and feelings of leaving Hong Kong for some years and settling in a country where the language, culture and climate are vastly different from home, and brush it off with a generic ESL textbook-like answer. But how are they, really? This documentary originated from the ‘We Are Hongkongers’ research project, funded by the British Academy/Wolfson Fellowship. Eleven Hongkongers who have moved to the UK since 2019 participated in sharing their experiences and feelings in multiple filmed visits. This film features a few of these participants’ stories. Followed by a panel discussion with co-director Sui-Ting Kong, Tsang Chi-ho of nowhere UK 飛地英國, and Mona Jamil, community-oriented organiser and civic engagement lead at the Migration Museum. English subtitles for the deaf and hard of hearing (SDH). British Sign Language (BSL) interpretation provided for post-screening discussion. Content warning: This work contains footage of police violence at protest scenes and strong language which some individuals may find distressing.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-concepc.description: This captivating documentary by Jochi Melero and Carlos Larrieu explores the life and legacy of César Concepción (1909-1974), a maestro of La Plena, and trailblazer in Latin music. Featuring rare performances, personal interviews with Gilberto Santa Rosa, Danny Rivera, Rafael Ithier, Frank Grillo “Machito” and other iconic figures of his era, it brings his contributions to life while showcasing the timeless power of his music.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-strawbe.description: David, a university student, meets Diego, an openly gay intellectual with a passion for art and literature. What begins as an unlikely encounter gradually develops into a deep and unexpected friendship that challenges David's assumptions and changes both of their lives in 1970s Havana. This screening will be followed by an in-person Q&A with Cuban actor Jorge Perugorria.

https://www.ica.art/films/hkff-forms-of-.description: A programme of experimental documentary, artists’ moving image and lecture performance explores voices as both fragile and impossible to fully erase. Traces endure as bodies, images and technologies become sites where histories and memories are reactivated against systems that seek to silence them. A 45-minute screening is followed by an approximately 45-minute interactive lecture performance. Followed by in-person conversation with Rico Wong and Winnie Soon, moderated by Sun Park, Programme and Communications Manager at LUX. UK Premiere Confidential Records: Execution Hong Kong | 2019 | 4’ | Colour | In English with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Vvzela Kook 曲淵澈 A sci-fi reimagining of the demolished Kowloon Walled City, utilising old memories and scientific prediction to build a fantasized underground city for the defence of human beings. UK Premiere Compact Disc Hong Kong, UK | 2026 | 38’ | Colour | In Cantonese with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Rico Wong 王樂堯 After years of silence, the director and his friends return to fragments of a shared youth shaped by imprisonment, friendship and pixelated images that refuse to settle, searching for how to live with what remains. Winner of the CPH:DOX 2026 New:Vision Award and the TIDF 2026 Visionary Award Grand Prize. UK Premiere The Singing Fern Hong Kong | 2026 | 3’ | Colour | No Dialogue with Chinese and English subtitles Dir.: Au Wah Yan 區華欣 Beginning as a fictional fern-hunting party, rooted in Victorian pteridomania, the hunt turns inward — for undertone voices, unsettling emotions, and the unconscious mind. Lecture Performance：The Poetics of the Unerasable Artist: Winnie Soon 孫詠怡 As algorithmic curation habituates us to online erasure, this lecture performance frames erasure as a generative act — examining how obscured data continues to inhabit the digital landscape and navigating the boundary between enforced and self-imposed censorship. The session closes with a participatory book-binding action, inviting audiences to assemble a collective book from traces.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-quba.description: Against the backdrop of Havana’s sun-drenched streets and shimmering coastline, ¡Quba! explores the evolution of Cuba’s LGBTQ+ community through the stories of those who have fought for greater visibility and acceptance. At its heart is Adela Hernández, a pioneering trans politician and the first openly transgender person elected to public office in Cuba. Alongside her is Ramón Silverio, who transformed El Mejunje into a cultural space for LGBTQ+ artists and performers. Through archival footage and personal stories, the film follows generations of artists and activists as they challenge prejudice and celebrate the ongoing journey towards greater visibility and equality in Cuba, culminating in Cuba’s 2022 marriage equality referendum.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-nunkui.description: Guided by dreams and ancestral wisdom, a 13-year-old Shuar girl discovers her identity while her Amazonian community struggles to protect its land from mining.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-stories.description: This programme brings together four short films exploring the theme of resilience. Across different contexts and forms, the films consider resilience as the capacity to move through what does not work, and to adapt to life’s challenges rather than remaining in a static state. Through acts of rebellion, resistance and fighting for what we value in the face of repression, as well as through creativity and joy, these films explore the different ways we find strength, agency and ways forward. Programme Pharmacies ( Farmacias ), dir. Martín Montellano, Mexico 2025 Collective Memory ( Memoria Colectiva ), dir. Cristina Colmenares, Colombia, Peru 2025 Quebrante , dir. Janaina Wagner, Brazil 2024 Cold Water ( Agua Fría ), dir. Meme Cabello, Chile 2025 Total runtime: 82 min.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-perros-.description: The Saldaña family has new tasks for the summer: looking after the dog and the house of the Pernas, their neighbours. The house is a small luxury that provokes the envy of the neighbourhood, and the Saldañas, taking advantage of their duties as improvised caretakers, will live out their own vacation in it. The unexpected disappearance of the dog will be the trigger for a violent, miserable, and psychological confrontation between both families.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-los-cam.description: Inspired by true events, this story intertwines a crime thriller with a migrant drama. In 2010, Chinese mafias arrived in the city of Mendoza, which became the hidden stage of a silent war between two factions fighting for control of organised crime, operating in the shadows of a migrant community marked by silence, fear, and cultural distance. While Chinese community shopkeepers are extorted and women brought from China under false promises are forced into prostitution, the small family restaurant of the Dagengs unknowingly becomes the epicentre of this struggle. An anonymous complaint linked to the restaurant also sparks a judicial investigation that sets in motion the dismantling of the network through wiretaps. Prosecutor Diana Belenguer, determined to confront these criminal organisations, leads an unprecedented investigation in the country. With the help of Li, a Chinese-born police officer who translates wiretaps in Cantonese dialect, they begin to uncover the inner workings of the mafia, its codes, and its invisible hierarchies. The intercepted conversations not only expose the crimes but also reveal a family conflict within one of the mafias, marked by the tension between two brothers. Xu, a soldier of one of the organisations, decides to defy his clan and free a young victim known as La Pujianesa. That decision makes him a target of his own comrades, especially of Kwan, his older brother and a leader within the organisation, now tasked with killing him. As Xu and the young woman run for their lives, Prosecutor Belenguer and Officer Li delve into a criminal network far more extensive and complex than they had ever imagined.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-life-is.director: Eirene Houston & Hugo Ernesto Rivalta Castro
https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-life-is.description: Life is Dance follows the stories of six main protagonists, across 3 generations. Ordinary Cubans with one thing in common, their love of dance. Marta and Félix are nostalgic for the dance halls of old but still dance whenever they can. Damaris and Gusmel, are leaders of a small town dance group, it means everything to them to win the annual dance competition. Teenagers Lachy and Dayan would love to be professional dancers, if only they could just dance reggaeton and not have to learn the ‘old people’s dances.’ Full colour and music, disappointment and joy, we join these charismatic characters on their journey.

https://www.ica.art/films/lolaff-naira.description: Naira, an imaginative nine-year-old girl living in precarious conditions near the Colca Canyon, desperately seeks a way to save her mother, Nieves, from the cruel abuse of their landlord, Don Demetrio. When Nieves confesses that they can only escape with either money or wings, Naira clings to an ancient legend about men transforming into birds. After receiving what a shaman interprets as a divine sign from the god Inti – a condor feather – the young girl embarks on a race against time. With her mother's health worsening and Demetrio's threat looming, Naira sets out to secretly build a pair of wings from wool and feathers for the impending day of the solstice, determined to take flight toward freedom.
